dependencies.status_note: In Landeshauptstadt Wiesbaden, C-61/22, EU:C:2024:251, the Court declared Regulation (EU) 2019/1157 invalid and maintained its effects until a successor entered into force, subject to a maximum date of 31 December 2026. Regulation (EU) 2025/1208 entered into force on 10 July 2025, ending that effects-maintenance period. Under the successor, Article 7 governs format, titles and field-10 codes; Article 8 sets a general 3 August 2026 transition date and a conditional derogation to 3 August 2031 for specified existing cards. As of this review, the general date has passed. The Bulgarian national citation, fee linkage, implementation evidence and status of particular cards remain unreconciled.
successor_relevant_provisions: Article 7(2) (card title and standardized data-field-10 code)
dependencies.national_concordance: The Bulgarian EUR-Lex text of Regulation 2025/1208 Article 7(2) uses the same Bulgarian field-10 codes as Bulgarian EU-citizen Act Article 12(1) and Additional Provisions § 1(4)-(5). Article 12(11) separately refers to the 1030/2002 uniform format, which Article 7(1) of the successor also requires, but the reviewed national text does not establish application of the successor's implementing decisions or confirm the required card title on current cards. The Act's Article 10 and definitions still cite Regulation 2019/1157, and Article 12(11)'s fee comparison still names that regulation.
dependencies.transition_note: Bulgarian Personal Documents Act transitional § 24(3), in the MVR-hosted consolidation through SG 52/2025, says covered residence cards not meeting Article 7 of Regulation 2019/1157 are valid through 3 August 2026 unless they expire earlier. Regulation 2025/1208 Article 8(2)(b) permits a conditional later date through expiry or 3 August 2031 for cards satisfying specified ICAO and Annex criteria. The effect of the national provision, any later amendment or administrative instruction, and the status of individual cards require human/legal review; do not infer validity from this register.

dependencies.status_note: The MVR government consolidation is accepted through SG 52/2025. Articles 23, 25, 27–30 were compared with Directive 2004/38 Articles 15 and 27–33, using the shared-core Directive text. The national Act contains corresponding personal-conduct, individual-factor, threat, health, notice, appeal, departure-period and review provisions. Specific questions remain: Article 26 uses an alternative “data” formulation for national-security/public-order bans; Article 24(1)(4) permits health-based withdrawal; Article 25(2) uses “exceptional cases connected with national security” for the 10-year rule and protects minors where expulsion is in their interest; Article 27(3) ties the sub-month departure exception to a continuing threat; Article 28 suspends enforcement except for national-security grounds; and Article 30 measures the three-year lifting period from finality, while Directive Article 32 refers to enforcement of the final exclusion order. These wording and timing differences require legal interpretation and do not by themselves establish incompatibility.

The national text contains retained-residence routes after death/departure or relationship termination, five-year and early worker permanent-residence routes, absence rules, document issuance, and two-year absence provisions. Open interpretation questions include the precise relationship categories, the education-based child route, Article 17 absence periods, proof of continuous residence, whether document withdrawal changes an underlying right, and the applicant groups/timing for Articles 16(5) and 19(2)–(5).
